scenarios.label: SSP1-2.6 — rapid decarbonisation
scenarios.description: Net-zero around 2075. Forcing peaks mid-century then declines.

scenarios.label: SSP2-4.5 — current policy drift
scenarios.description: Roughly where stated policy lands. The engine's default.

scenarios.label: SSP3-7.0 — regional rivalry
scenarios.description: Weak coordination, high land-use emissions, no decline this century.

scenarios.label: SSP5-8.5 — fossil-fuelled growth
scenarios.description: High end. Retained as a tail-pricing stress case, not a central view.

problems: Step change of -0.50 degC around 1940 that the climate model cannot explain — most likely a station move or instrument change, not weather.

perils.label: High wind
perils.description: Daily mean wind at or above 10.3 m/s (23 mph). Gusts on such a day run well past 40 mph, which is where lifts, rigging and marine ops stop. Set on daily mean because that is the quantity GHCN-Daily reports and therefore the one a contract can settle on.

perils.label: Snow drought
perils.description: Under 24 in of snowfall in a rolling 30-day window. The existential risk for a ski operator.

perils.label: Warm snowline
perils.description: Base-area max above 4C, when falling precipitation arrives as rain and snowmaking stops.

perils.label: Rain day
perils.description: A single day clearing 0.35 in. The point where outdoor attendance measurably drops.

perils.label: Washout day
perils.description: 0.80 in in a day. Past this the day is generally lost, not just degraded.

perils.label: Extreme heat
perils.description: Daily maximum at or above 95F. The Bible's point about nonlinearity applies here hard.

perils.label: Hard freeze
perils.description: Minimum at or below 28F. Bud-break frost risk for vineyards and orchards.
